title: Scalar-adjunction transpose of a compact-support mixed-coefficient map
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$, and let $f:X\to Y$ have a compactification $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow hY$, with all three schemes separated of finite type over $k$, $j$ open and $h$ proper. Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories on small pro-etale sites; put $F_{f,R}=Rh_{*,R}j_{!,R}$ for $R=A,B$. Write $T_Z=-\otimes^L_{A_Z}B_Z$ and $\operatorname{Res}_Z$ for the derived extension/exact restriction adjunction, with counit $\epsilon_Z:T_Z\operatorname{Res}_Z\to1$. Let $K\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $L\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, meaning bounded intrinsically constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude, and let $t:K\to\operatorname{Res}_XL$ be any derived morphism. Write $t^\sharp:T_XK\to L$ for its scalar-adjunction transpose. Use the canonical comparison $d_f:F_{f,A}\operatorname{Res}_X\simeq\operatorname{Res}_YF_{f,B}$ from [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] and the counit-normalized $b_f:T_YF_{f,A}\to F_{f,B}T_X$ of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Then
$$\bigl(d_f(L)\circ F_{f,A}(t)\bigr)^\sharp=F_{f,B}(t^\sharp)\circ b_f(K).$$
Equivalently, the scalar-extension mate of $d_f$ has the specified proper-counit and open-tensor normalization $b_f$, including its counit equation
$$\epsilon_Y(F_{f,B}L)\circ T_Y(d_f(L))=F_{f,B}(\epsilon_X(L))\circ b_f(\operatorname{Res}_XL).$$
In this last formula $b_f$ denotes the same counit-defined transformation on the ambient derived categories; invertibility is required only on $\Dctf$ input. The equality is natural in $K,L,t$, requires no flatness of $B$ over $A$, and is compatible with two successive coefficient homomorphisms and their tensor associators. An identity coefficient homomorphism gives the original map $F_{f,A}(t)$; when $t$ is also the identity the resulting map is the identity.

proof.text:
Put $Z=\overline X$, $R_R=Rh_{*,R}$, $J_R=j_{!,R}$, and abbreviate scalar restriction by $r$. The proper counit square and representative identification of [lem-sp-proper-scalar-counit-square] give $D$ and $\gamma$; [lem-sp-open-scalar-counit-square] gives $a,E$ and $\epsilon_ZJ_B\,T_Z(a)=J_B(\epsilon_X)E_r$. The specified restriction comparison is $d_f=D J_B\circ R_A(a)$ by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], while $b_f=R_B(E)\gamma J_A$ by [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], with its ambient natural construction specified in [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison]. Proper naturality at $a_L$ now gives
$$\epsilon_YF_BL\,T_Y(d_f(L))=R_B(\epsilon_ZJ_BL\,T_Z(a_L))\gamma_{J_Ar_XL}=F_B(\epsilon_XL)b_f(r_XL).$$

proof.text:
The scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] gives $v^\sharp=\epsilon T(v)$. Expand the left side and apply Step 1 and naturality of $b_f$:
$$(d_f(L)F_A(t))^\sharp=F_B(\epsilon_XL)b_f(r_XL)T_YF_A(t)=F_B(\epsilon_XL\,T_X(t))b_f(K).$$
This is the required formula. Naturality of the Hom bijections, $d_f$ and $b_f$ gives naturality in $K,L,t$. Conversely take $K=r_XL,t=1$ in this ambient calculation to recover the counit equation. No Tor assertion about $r_XL$ is used. Invertibility only on ctf input is [det-sp-reduction-direct-image].

proof.text:
For $A\to B\to C$, the composite scalar counit is $\epsilon^{B,C}T^{B,C}(\epsilon^{A,B})$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] this is the direct counit under $\alpha$ of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]; hence successive transposes equal the direct transpose precomposed with $\alpha$. The $d_f$ compose by [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], and [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] gives
$$b_{A,C}(K)\alpha_{F_AK}=F_C(\alpha_K)b_{B,C}(T_X^{A,B}K)T_Y^{B,C}(b_{A,B}(K)).$$
Substitution in Step 2 identifies respectively the input maps, transposes and comparison factors for successive versus direct change. Scalar extension preserves ctf by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]; restricted objects remain ambient.

proof.text: For identity coefficients, the scalar adjunction is the identity under its canonical unitors [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. The open comparison is identity by [lem-sp-open-scalar-counit-square]; the proper comparison is identity by [lem-sp-proper-scalar-counit-square]: choose $I\xrightarrow{1}I$ for its K-injective resolution, so its inverse representative is $1$. Thus $d_f=1$, Step 1 gives $b_f=1$, and Step 2 gives $F_A(t)$, or $1$ if $t=1$. All counit squares and adjunctions above are ambient and allow nonflat coefficient maps.
